craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of workshop disputation — ends-first reasoning. No-will-no-wonders; grossness-never-good close. Rejected: (a) good→useful → killed: good is broader. Read aloud: SO with-NO-will TO-make … NEV-er WORLD-good.

lines: So with no will to make, no wonders made —
mere grossness would be, never world-good.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tathā cikīrṣāṃ ca vinā vicitraracanodbhavaḥ sthūlatāmātrameva syānna tu lokopayoginī

reads_against.argmap: Without desiring? → No will, no wonders: mere grossness, never world-good.
c1_essence: Potter necessary, nature watching, helpers insufficient, wisdom and will required, sufficiency tested (vv28-33).
Array excels by ends; Lord and un-Lord fenced off atomically; pradhāna will-less yet person-aim-ness stands (vv34-36).
